title: False-encoding taxonomy: how apparent SPK 'encoding' during Fig04 development was repeatedly generated by task/sampling structure rather than genuine neural representation
central_claim: decodability != representation of the intended variable. A classifier answers whether Y is predictable from X under the sampling scheme in use; it does not by itself establish that the neural signal represents the biological variable named Y. If a nuisance variable C covaries with both X and Y (X <- C -> Y), I(X;Y) > 0 can occur with no genuine neural code for Y.

rows.what_exposed_it: Finite-permutation audit: with B permutations the minimum representable p-value is 1/(B+1) (North et al. 2002); the original scripts used B=50 (context decoder) and B=100 (RSA) with no floor correction, so an exact-zero p-value was never actually supportable
rows.correct_interpretation: Significance had been systematically overstated by omitting the (1+k)/(N_PERM+1) finite-sample correction. Fixed by raising to N_PERM=999 with the correction applied throughout.

manuscript_paragraph_draft: During development of the SPK encoding analyses reported here, we encountered and corrected a sequence of distinct mechanisms by which apparently strong 'decoding' of a variable of interest can arise without that variable being genuinely represented in the neural signal. These included: decoding windows misaligned to the true event timing, which caused a decoder nominally targeting the omitted (expected) stimulus identity to substantially read out an actually-presented preceding stimulus; temporal/adaptation carryover, which can independently produce a similar spurious content signature; leakage across non-independent trials within the same temporal cycle under ungrouped cross-validation, which produced an apparently significant predictability-context decoder (4 of 12 area/slot cells surviving FDR correction) that collapsed entirely under cycle-grouped, leave-one-cycle-out cross-validation (0 of 11 cells, accuracy at or below chance); and an uncorrected finite-permutation floor, which understated several p-values as exactly zero. We report this sequence explicitly because each mechanism independently generated a convincing but false positive, and because the general principle -- that statistical decodability of Y from neural activity X does not by itself establish that X represents the biologically intended variable Y, particularly when a nuisance variable may covary with both -- is a broadly applicable caution for population decoding in this literature. All corrected estimates reported in the main results were required to survive canonical event timing, matched analysis windows, group-safe (cycle-level) cross-validation, a within-group-exchangeable permutation null with a finite-sample-corrected p-value floor, and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction across the relevant test family.
